label: M4ntis
context: M4ntis is a platform designed to bridge the gap between visual algorithmic trading strategy development and real-time hardware execution, specifically targeting the limitations of general-purpose software in modern financial markets. The core purpose is to empower traders and financial professionals, even those lacking extensive coding expertise, to deploy sophisticated trading strategies directly onto custom-designed hardware. The system architecture is a hybrid approach, combining a visual drag-and-drop interface for strategy creation with a custom 27-opcode CPU implemented on a Real Digital Urbana board (Xilinx Spartan-7 FPGA). The frontend, built using Next.js and ReactFlow, provides the visual canvas for users to construct their trading logic, which is then compiled down to the custom instruction set. A Node.js streaming backend connects the frontend to an LLM API, facilitating strategy explanation and refinement. The backend leverages FastAPI and Python for API development and data processing, interacting with a PostgreSQL database (potentially using TimescaleDB for time-series data). The custom CPU, implemented in Verilog, incorporates native trading primitives such as price history reading from circular buffers, moving average calculations, threshold comparisons, and balance tracking, all designed for single-cycle execution. The compiled strategies are deployed to the FPGA via UART in milliseconds, enabling rapid iteration and real-time execution. The FPGA receives live price ticks and streams execution decisions and account balances back to the web interface, providing a live dashboard for monitoring. The data flow begins with users constructing visual workflows in the frontend, which are then compiled into the custom instruction set. This instruction set is executed on the FPGA, which processes real-time market data and generates trading signals. These signals are then transmitted back to the frontend for display and monitoring. The team, consisting of four members, achieved a significant accomplishment by successfully designing, verifying, and closing hardware timing for a custom trading CPU on an FPGA, demonstrating a 60% accuracy rate outperforming the baseline Maia model. The project involved 364 source files, highlighting the complexity of the integrated hardware and software system. The development process emphasized the importance of simulation versus hardware realities, the precision of specifications, and the challenges of full-stack scope, particularly balancing the web UI, LLM analysis, data normalization, and serial protocols down to custom hardware. The project's future direction includes completing hardware bring-up with live tick feeds, running full multi-indicator strategies, and expanding the CPU architecture for concurrent symbol handling and increased throughput.
